ka.name: Georgian
ka.fact: Georgian script is unrelated to any other alphabet in the world.

hy.name: Armenian
hy.fact: The alphabet was created by Mesrop Mashtots in 405 - it is over 1,600 years old.

el.name: Greek
el.fact: The first alphabet in history with letters for vowels.

he.name: Hebrew
he.fact: Dead for almost 2,000 years - and revived as a spoken language in the 20th century.

ar.name: Arabic
ar.fact: Written right to left; vowels are barely shown in writing.

fa.name: Persian (Farsi)
fa.fact: An Indo-European language, yet written in Arabic script.

ur.name: Urdu
ur.fact: A close relative of Hindi - but written in Persian script.

hi.name: Hindi
hi.fact: Devanagari script: the letters hang from a shared line on top.

bn.name: Bengali
bn.fact: Spoken by over 270 million people - top 6 in the world.

ta.name: Tamil
ta.fact: Alive for over 2,000 years almost unchanged - a classical language of India.

si.name: Sinhala
si.fact: The language of Sri Lanka, with almost round letters.

th.name: Thai
th.fact: Five tones and no spaces between words.

lo.name: Lao
lo.fact: Similar to Thai, but the letters are noticeably rounder.

km.name: Khmer
km.fact: The Khmer alphabet has 74 letters - the longest in the world.

my.name: Burmese
my.fact: Circle letters: drawn on palm leaves so as not to tear the fibres.

vi.name: Vietnamese
vi.fact: Latin script with diacritics, devised by French missionaries.

ko.name: Korean
ko.fact: Hangul was invented by scholars in 1443 - it is called the most logical alphabet.

ja.name: Japanese
ja.fact: The only language that uses three writing systems at once.

zh.name: Chinese
zh.fact: One character = one syllable and one meaning. Learning to read takes years.

mn.name: Mongolian
mn.fact: Cyrillic with two extra letters - but the traditional script is written top to bottom.

am.name: Amharic
am.fact: The official language of Ethiopia, with its own Ge'ez script.

fi.name: Finnish
fi.fact: 15 grammatical cases and record-breaking long words.

et.name: Estonian
et.fact: 14 cases - and that is not the record among its neighbours.

hu.name: Hungarian
hu.fact: Not Indo-European: its closest relatives are Khanty and Mansi.

cs.name: Czech
cs.fact: The letter ř exists only in Czech - foreigners can't pronounce it.

pl.name: Polish
pl.fact: Words like «szczęście» - a championship of consonants in a row.

ro.name: Romanian
ro.fact: A Romance language surrounded on all sides by Slavic ones.

tr.name: Turkish
tr.fact: The letter ğ («soft g») is not pronounced at all.

az.name: Azerbaijani
az.fact: The letter ə is the «schwa» sound, a rare guest in alphabets.

is.name: Icelandic
is.fact: The letter þ is a direct heir of the runes. The Vikings' language has barely changed.

cy.name: Welsh
cy.fact: The combination ll is a sound found almost nowhere else.

ga.name: Irish
ga.fact: An official EU language spoken daily by fewer than 100,000 people.

mt.name: Maltese
mt.fact: The only Semitic language in the EU - and the only one written in Latin script.

eu.name: Basque
eu.fact: A language isolate: it has no proven relatives at all.

la.name: Latin
la.fact: A dead language - yet officially alive in the Vatican.

eo.name: Esperanto
eo.fact: Zamenhof's constructed language (1887) - the most successful ever invented.

sw.name: Swahili
sw.fact: The lingua franca of East Africa, spoken in 10+ countries.
